24×24 footings may look like overkill, but footing size is about more than just the size of the house. Here are 5 things to know: Soil conditions matter — The ground has to support everything above it. Width spreads the load — A wider footing distributes weight over more soil. Depth matters too — Footing depth can depend on design, soil, grade, and local requirements. Reinforcement matters — Properly placed rebar helps the footing perform as designed. Follow the engineered plans — Bigger isn't automatically better; the footing should match the structural design. The foundation is one place where I'd rather understand why it's designed that way before changing anything. Would you consider 24×24 overkill for a residential build? #Footings #Foundation #Concrete #HomeBuilding #OzareLegacyLand

The key to a strong and stable structure lies beneath the surface. Let’s dig into the fascinating world of footings! 🔍 🌐 Footing Fundamentals: Footing is the unsung hero of construction, responsible for transferring the weight of a building to the solid ground below. It’s a game-changer! But how do you choose the right type of footing? 🤔 ✅ Factors to Consider: 1️⃣ Depth of Safe-Bearing Strata 2️⃣ Soil Type & Condition 3️⃣ Superstructure’s Needs 🏠 Isolated Footing: When you’ve got single columns standing solo, isolated footings are your go-to choice. These footings ensure stability, prevent sinking, and keep things safe and sound. 💰 Cost-Effective Choice: Isolated footings are often the budget-friendly option, especially when the ground’s properties remain consistent. Now, let’s talk types of isolated footings: 1️⃣ Pad Footing: Versatile in shape, efficient, but watch out for lateral forces! What’s your preference – circular, rectangular, or square? 2️⃣ Sloped Footing: Less concrete, less reinforcement, and a sleek 45-degree slope. It’s all about maintaining that perfect angle! 📐 3️⃣ Stepped Footing: A classic approach for residential buildings, although it’s become less common in recent years. 🏘️ 4️⃣ Combined Footing: When space is tight, and individual footings won’t cut it, we combine forces! 💪 What’s your experience with footings? The challenge is that once the pavers are installed, the concrete footings completely disappear underneath them.
